verdict: REVISE. The load-bearing conclusion holds and is strengthened: independently rebuilt and reran the spike (5 fresh processes, three-way pattern reproduces byte-for-byte), and the reentrant DocumentSource.Custom call does genuine per-instance typecheck work, never a 2-4ms warm cache hit -- Q010's inherited 'benign cache-hit / already-resolved by the SourceFiles walk' hypothesis is decisively ruled out, and stays ruled out warm, at a 3rd reentrant call, and under reversed order. But 02-results.md's headline framing outruns its evidence and must not be cited forward, which is why REVISE not SHIP. Added a control spike (artifacts/q027-control, same FCS 43.9.101 pin, 7 modes x 5 processes; raw log artifacts/review-logs/control-runs.txt) that decomposes the reentrantA=516ms number: (1) ~91% of it is one-time first-typecheck-in-process cost (JIT / FCS static init / referenced-assembly reads) -- reentrantA is literally the FIRST check in the process while coldA runs 5th, fully warm; a throwaway warmup project collapses reentrantA to ~48ms and reentrantB to ~17ms, both BELOW cold, landing exactly on the design's own pre-registered REVISE outcome ('between cold and warm'). (2) A direct, NON-reentrant first check on the same checker costs ~929ms -- MORE than the reentrant 516ms -- so the executor's inference that 'reentrantA > cold indicates reentrancy overhead on top of first-touch cost' is backwards: the outer ParseAndCheckProject pre-builds the shared project snapshot, so the reentrant call is CHEAPER than a from-cold direct check, not more expensive. (3) The cold baseline is also not apples-to-apples: it used keepAssemblyContents=false while the checker under test used true (~26ms/20% of the residual gap). (4) The A-vs-B asymmetry the executor left as unexplained inference is a call-ORDER amortization effect, not a file-identity property -- reverse mode (B first, A second) gives B=~597ms, A=~10ms; a 3rd call keeps decreasing (528>82>24ms) without ever collapsing to warm. Net: the mechanism claim (reentrant queries do real, order-amortized work on an already-warm shared snapshot) is intact and sharper; the 'reentrant is more expensive than cold / reentrancy overhead' magnitude framing is an artifact of two uncontrolled variables and a backwards inference. Cite the warmed ~17-48ms numbers, not the raw first-in-process ~516ms. Still open (unchanged): literal concurrency of the outer walk (no thread instrumentation, by design), cross-file-dependent content, scale beyond 3-4 files, and any real FSAC editing session. New cross-cutting caution for the lineage: any single 'first check' latency reported by a prior quartet carries the same ~400-500ms one-time JIT/init tax and should be re-read with that in mind. See 03-review.md.
